content: 1. Clarithromycin and Eucalyptus: Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of eucalyptus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended. 2. Clarithromycin and Everolimus: Clarithromycin significantly increases everolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. This combination is contraindicated. 3. Clarithromycin and Ezogabine: Both drugs can prolong the QT interval, especially at higher doses of ezogabine (e.g., 1200 mg/day). QT interval monitoring is essential when co-administered. 4. Clarithromycin and Fedratinib: Clarithromycin increases fedratinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the fedratinib dose to 200 mg/day and adjust as needed upon discontinuation of clarithromycin. 5. Clarithromycin and Felbamate: Clarithromycin increases felbamate levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 6. Clarithromycin and Felodipine: Clarithromycin increases felodipine levels, potentially causing hypotension, edema, bradycardia, and acute kidney injury. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Clarithromycin and Fentanyl (all forms): Clarithromycin increases fentanyl levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, raising the risk of respiratory depression and sedation. Avoid or use alternatives. If co-administration is necessary, monitor patients closely and adjust fentanyl doses as needed. 8. Clarithromycin and Fesoterodine: Clarithromycin increases fesoterodine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 9. Clarithromycin and Fexinidazole: Clarithromycin decreases fexinidazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QT interval. Avoid or use alternatives. 10. Clarithromycin and Fexofenadine: Clarithromycin increases fexofenadine levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. The clinical significance is unclear, but close monitoring is advised. 11. Clarithromycin and Finasteride: Clarithromycin increases finasteride levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Clarithromycin and Finerinone: Clarithromycin significantly increases finerinone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. This combination is contraindicated. 13. Clarithromycin and Fingolimod: Both drugs prolong the QT interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 14. Clarithromycin and Flecainide: Both drugs prolong the QT interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 15. Clarithromycin and Flibanserin: Clarithromycin increases flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of severe hypotension or syncope. 16. Clarithromycin and Fluconazole: Both drugs prolong the QT interval. Fluconazole also increases clarithromycin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor closely. 17. Clarithromycin and Fludrocortisone: Clarithromycin increases fludrocortisone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition and P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Clarithromycin and Fluoxetine: Both drugs prolong the QT interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 19. Clarithromycin and Fluphenazine: Both drugs prolong the QT interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 20. Clarithromycin and Flurazepam: Clarithromycin increases flurazepam levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Clarithromycin and Fluticasone (all forms): Clarithromycin increases fluticasone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, potentially leading to systemic corticosteroid adverse effects such as Cushing's syndrome. Avoid or use alternatives for intranasal forms; monitor closely for inhaled forms. 22. Clarithromycin and Fluvastatin: Clarithromycin increases the risk of myopathy when combined with fluvastatin due to OATP1B1 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 23. Clarithromycin and Fluvoxamine: Both drugs prolong the QT interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 24. Clarithromycin and Fondaparinux: Clarithromycin increases fondaparinux effects by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 25. Clarithromycin and Formoterol: Both drugs prolong the QT interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 26. Clarithromycin and Fosamprenavir: Clarithromycin increases fosamprenavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor closely. 27. Clarithromycin and Fosaprepitant: Clarithromycin increases fosaprepitant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor closely. 28. Clarithromycin and Foscarnet: Both drugs prolong the QT interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 29. Clarithromycin and Fosphenytoin: Fosphenytoin decreases clarithromycin levels via CYP3A4 induction. Monitor closely. 30. Clarithromycin and Fostamatinib: Clarithromycin increases fostamatinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, potentially increasing toxicities. Monitor closely and adjust fostamatinib doses as needed. 31. Clarithromycin and Fostemsavir: Both drugs prolong the QT interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 32. Clarithromycin and Futibatinib: Clarithromycin increases futibatinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 33. Clarithromycin and Gadobenate: Both drugs prolong the QT interval. This combination is contraindicated. 34. Clarithromycin and Ganaxolone: Clarithromycin affects ganaxolone metabolism via CYP3A4 inhibition. The clinical significance is unclear, but close monitoring is advised. 35. Clarithromycin and Gefitinib: Clarithromycin increases gefitinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, raising the risk of adverse effects. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 36. Clarithromycin and Gemifloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QT interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 37. Clarithromycin and Gemtuzumab: Both drugs prolong the QT interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Clarithromycin and Gentamicin: Clarithromycin increases gentamicin levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Clarithromycin and Gepirone: Clarithromycin increases gepirone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Both drugs also prolong the QT interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 40. Clarithromycin and Gilteritinib: Clarithromycin increases gilteritinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Both drugs also prolong the QT interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 41. Clarithromycin and Givinostat: Both drugs prolong the QT interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 42. Clarithromycin and Glasdegib: Clarithromycin increases glasdegib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Both drugs also prolong the QT interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 43. Clarithromycin and Glecaprevir/Pibrentasvir: Clarithromycin increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Clarithromycin and Glimepiride, Glipizide, Glyburide: Clarithromycin increases the levels of these drugs via plasma protein binding competition, increasing the risk of hypoglycemia. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Clarithromycin and Goserelin: Goserelin increases clarithromycin toxicity by prolonging the QT interval, raising the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Clarithromycin and Granisetron: Both drugs prolong the QT interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 47. Clarithromycin and Grapefruit: Grapefruit increases clarithromycin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. The clinical significance is unclear, but close monitoring is advised. 48. Clarithromycin and Griseofulvin: Griseofulvin decreases clarithromycin levels via CYP3A4 induction. The clinical significance is unclear, but close monitoring is advised. 49. Clarithromycin and Guanfacine: Clarithromycin increases guanfacine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce guanfacine dosage by half for extended-release forms. Monitor closely. 50. Clarithromycin and Haloperidol: Clarithromycin increases haloperidol levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Both drugs also prolong the QT interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 51. Clarithromycin and Heparin: Clarithromycin increases heparin effects by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 52. Clarithromycin and Histrelin: Histrelin increases clarithromycin toxicity by prolonging the QT interval, raising the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Clarithromycin and Hydrocodone: Clarithromycin increases hydrocodone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, raising the risk of fatal respiratory depression. Monitor closely. 54. Clarithromycin and Hydrocortisone: Clarithromycin increases hydrocortisone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition and P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Clarithromycin and Hydroxychloroquine: Both drugs prolong the QT interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs.
